thread:
Samir K: heads-up, running into a type mismatch only when building for the edge worker sample. Works in node but esbuild fails types.

Samir K: TS error: "Type 'any' is not assignable to type 'unknown'" originating from SDK types for createClient overloads.

Lina V: can you paste the import and the exact signature line that errors?

Samir K: import line: `import Redwood from '@redwood-inference/sdk'`
Code spot where it fails: `const client = Redwood.createClient({ apiKey: process.env.RI_KEY })`
The d.ts shows two overloads: `createClient<T = unknown>(opts: ClientOptions): Client<T>` and `createClient(opts: ClientOptions & { forceAny?: true }): Client<any>` and the edge build picks the first one for some reason.

Marco D: edge bundlers (esbuild/vite) and TS moduleResolution differences can choose a different .d.ts path if the package uses conditional exports. If the package's exports map points to `./dist/edge/index.mjs` without a matching types entry, TS might fall back to a different declaration file that uses `unknown` generics.

Lina V: quick hacks: 1) add a local ambient declaration in your project to narrow the overload (`declare module '@redwood-inference/sdk' { export function createClient<T = any>(opts: any): any }`) — not great but fast. 2) enable `skipLibCheck: true` to ignore the transitive mismatch. 3) prefer named import `import { createClient } from '@redwood-inference/sdk'` which sometimes resolves different type paths.

Samir K: tried named import, still same. Adding ambient module made the TS error go away. Runtime is fine.

SDK-bot: FYI the SDK currently publishes two .d.ts bundles: `types/index.d.ts` and `types/edge.d.ts`. There's a known mismatch when bundlers pick the ESM entry without typesExports. See https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/987

Marco D: long-term fix: SDK should add `types` and `exports.types` entries in package.json and ensure the conditional exports include a types mapping for edge vs node. Also keep overloads aligned between bundles (avoid different default generic bounds).

CI Bot: created issue RDW-1132 to add an end-to-end edge types smoke test in CI.

Samir K: for the sample, i'll add a small local `types/overrides.d.ts` with the narrowed signature and mention the caveats in the sample README. Thanks all :raised_hands: 

Lina V: also consider adding a short section in devex docs: "TS config for edge samples" with recommended flags: `moduleResolution: 'bundler'`, `esModuleInterop: true` (if using default imports), and `skipLibCheck: true` as a temporary shim.

Marco D: agree. We'll follow up with SDK team to harmonize the type exports and remove the need for these shims.
